summary: Frontend-only verification of chevron/title overlap fix on /eventos page (3rd attempt). Tested BOTH FESTIVAL and PREMIER tabs across 8 viewport widths (320, 375, 640, 768, 1024, 1280, 1440, 1920). All 16 combinations PASS. No text clipping (scrollWidth == clientWidth for both month and word in all cases), no chevron/title overlap (left chevron right edge < month/word left edge, right chevron left edge > month/word right edge in every case), reasonable gap maintained (4px at 320px, growing to 132px at 1920px). Confirmed tab switching re-renders correctly without reload. Regression checks passed: category boxes render (festival-cat-0 and premier-even-0 have valid non-overlapping boxes at 320px), TabsBar labels FESTIVAL/EVENTOS/PREMIER render on single line at 320px (sw==cw, height ~17px, no wrap). Screenshots at 375px (FESTIVAL) and 1280px (Premier) visually confirm correct layout with chevrons flanking title cleanly.
critical_code_review_comments: Fix is stable: grid-cols-[auto_1fr_auto] on mobile with scale-[0.5] chevrons gives central column ~172px at 320px which comfortably fits 'DICIEMBRE' and 'FESTIVAL' at clamp(1.6rem, 5vw, 4rem)/(1.3rem,6.5vw,5rem).
whitespace-nowrap + overflow-x-hidden on wrapper prevents both wrapping and horizontal scrollbar leak.
Suggest adding a Playwright regression test for these viewports so future edits don't reintroduce the bug.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Verified via bounding-box math (not just screenshots) that chevrons never overlap title text and text never clips container at 320/375/640/768/1024/1280/1440/1920 for both festival ('OCTUBRE'/'FESTIVAL') and premier ('DICIEMBRE'/'Premier') tabs. Used window.scrollTo + 1500ms wait to avoid scroll-timing false negatives. Data: month='octubre'/'diciembre', word='festival'/'Premier' (rendered lowercase by planeCrashSafe, cursive title-case for Premier).
rca of the issue: N/A - previously reported bug is not reproducible with current implementation. Root cause of prior failures was likely the equal grid columns (grid-cols-3) which forced the center column too narrow; current implementation uses auto_1fr_auto on mobile and 1fr_2.2fr_1fr on sm+ giving the central column enough width, combined with scale-[0.5] chevrons on mobile.
